defects.description: The rise from below 1% to above 2% of GDP is called 'a more than tenfold rise', but going from ~1% to ~2% is roughly a doubling, not tenfold.
paraphrases: 1% to 2% of GDP is about a doubling, not a tenfold rise.
A tenfold rise from 1% would be 10% of GDP, not 2%.
The stated growth multiple is far too high for 1%-to-2%.
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'a more than doubling' (~1% to ~2%). Findable from the two GDP shares, distinct.

defects.description: The top 1% is said to account for 'more than 60%' of spending, but the top 1% is a subset of the top 5%, which accounts for only about half — a subset cannot exceed the group that contains it.
paraphrases: The top 1% cannot exceed the top 5% (about half), so more than 60% is impossible.
A subset (top 1%) spending more than its superset (top 5%) is contradictory.
If the top 5% is almost half, the top 1% must be at most that, not over 60%.
defects.rationale: Correct value 'more than 20%' (top 1% share). Findable from the top-5% share, distinct.

defects.description: If the top 5% account for almost half of spending, the other 95% account for the remaining half, but the text says the other 95% account for 'just one-tenth'.
paraphrases: Almost half plus one-tenth does not add up to the whole.
If the top 5% take almost half, the rest take about half, not one-tenth.
The two shares do not sum to 100%.
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'the other half' (complement of almost half). Findable from the top-5% share, distinct.
